newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sandvik sees same 1997 result as in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Sandvik sees same 1997 result as in 1996.

text.p: Swedish engineering and specialty metals company Sandvik AB said on Tuesday it still forecast that its 1997 result would be the same as in 1996.
"The prior forecast of a largely unchanged profit after financial income and expenses in 1997 compared with 1996 remains valid," Sandvik said in a statement.

The company posted a 29 percent fall in profit to 941 million crowns after financial items for the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same 1996 period. Sales fell to 7.33 billion crowns from 7.42 billion.
Sandvik said in a statement that a weaker crown helped its order intake and invoicing.

"The Swedish crown was three percent weaker than in the first quarter of 1996 and five percent weaker than in the fourth quarter of 1996. This increased Sandvik's order intake and invoicing values as well as items in the balance sheet."

It said the effect on earnings would be slower since Sandvik hedges its exports from Sweden though forward exchange contracts. However, the rates were more favourable in the first quarter of 1996 than in the same 1997 period.
In its tooling division, its largest, invoiced sales rose to 2.47 billion crowns from 2.46 billion crowns. Operating income in the unit fell to 484 million crowns from 537 million crowns.
"Sandvik Tooling had lower invoiced sales than in the preceding year in Europe and in some markets in Asia," Sandvik said in a statement, adding that sales in North America continued to be strong.
In its steel division, invoiced sales fell to 2.39 billion crowns from 2.49 billion while operating profit fell to 231 million crowns from 413 million.

"Invoiced sales of Sandvik Steel at fixed exchange rates were higher than in the fourth quarter of 1996 but were eight percent below the high level at the beginning of 1996 due to lower prices," it said.
